question:
An engineer must implement a Cisco UCS system at a customer site. One of the requirements is to implement SAN boot. The storage system maps the source WWPN to a unique LUN.
Which method does Cisco recommend to configure the SAN boot?
options: Define the vHBAs as bootable and leave the boot target definition empty.
Create a SAN boot policy in which every initiator is mapped to a different target LUN.
Define the vHBAs as bootable and leave the default values on the boot target definition.
Create a SAN boot policy in which every initiator is mapped to the same target LUN.
theory: For SAN boot where the storage array presents the boot LUN by mapping the initiator's (vHBA's) source WWPN to a fixed LUN, Cisco's recommended practice is to build the SAN boot policy so that every initiator (each vHBA/path) is configured to point at the same target LUN ID, since the array itself differentiates access per-WWPN rather than needing different LUN numbers per path. Leaving boot targets undefined or using default values would not tell UCS Manager which specific LUN/target WWPN to boot from, and mapping each initiator to a different LUN would be incorrect when the array uses WWPN-based LUN mapping to a single logical boot volume. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Storage Management, SAN Boot Policies)
